LESSON: READING 6.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do people read short stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main ideas in the short story

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the main ideas in the short story
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the main ideas in the short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story.
4. Show that you can: identify the main ideas in the short story

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 6.4.1 Intensive Reading: short story important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.
